newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Transocean ASA posts 9-mo profit.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Transocean ASA posts 9-mo profit.

text.p: Norwegian drilling and offshore services company Transocean Drilling ASA said on Tuesday its nine-month after-tax result swung into a 433 million crowns ($68 million) profit from a loss of 105 million crowns in the same year-ago period.
A statement to the Oslo Bourse attributed the improved results to higher day rates for the company's offshore mobile rigs.
It was the last time that Transocean ASA reported a result. The company merged with U.S. group Sonat Offshore Drilling Inc in early September to form Transocean Offshore Inc.

Operating revenues grew marginally to 2.33 billion crowns, operation results increased to 184 million crowns from 43 million and the result before minorities and taxes went to a 446 million crwon profit from a loss of 94 million crowns.

Transocean ASA said the nine-month result included a profit of 332 million crowns from the sale of a stake in Anchor Drilling Fluids. The operating result in the third quarter included 56 million crowns in costs related to the merger with Sonat, it said.
The company said it expected day rates for most of its rigs to continue to rise.
It said Marathon Oil UK would lease mobile rig Transocean Explorer at considerably higher rates than today's rates.
Transocean gave no figures but said the contract was expected to take effect in April next year.
The deal covers four wells with an option for another well. It is expected to last 200 days with an option for another 40 days.

Transocean said Amoco had exercised an option for a six-month extension of the current 12-month leasing contract for Transocean Nordic. The rate is higher than the existing contract, Transocean said, again without giving any figures.
